headline: Ramsay Hall becomes a COVID-19 testing centre for Camden residents
detail: A partnership between UCL, the London Borough of Camden and the Department of Health and Social Care, increasing testing capacity for the borough rather than for UCL.
quote: UCL’s Ramsay Hall will become a COVID-19 testing centre from today, as part of a partnership between the London Borough of Camden and the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC).
notes: UCL estate used for the borough's testing, not its own. Distinct from the Bidborough House centre for UCL students and staff, which opened a fortnight later.

headline: Asymptomatic lateral flow testing opens for students at Bidborough House
detail: Part of the national testing programme for universities, to support travel over the winter break. Free, voluntary, results in about two hours.
quote: Asymptomatic COVID-19 testing for UCL students starts today, as part of the national testing programme for universities to support students to travel over the winter break.
notes: Reverses the position of 16 September, when asymptomatic testing was ruled out as a routine offer. It arrives as a national programme with a specific purpose: getting students home.

headline: Staff explicitly excluded from asymptomatic testing at its launch
quote: If you are a member of UCL staff, please do not book an appointment for an asymptomatic test. The Government has introduced the national testing programme specifically to support students who wish to leave university for the end of term.
notes: Matters for reading the case data: through December 2020 the staff and student series were produced under different testing regimes, so a comparison between them in that period is not like for like.

headline: Second national lockdown ends and London returns to Tier 2
quote: The current national lockdown period in England is due to end this Wednesday, 2 December, after which London will be in Tier 2 (High Alert) restrictions.
notes: London moved to Tier 3 on 16 December and Tier 4 on 20 December, neither of which the newsletters cover, because the last update before the winter break was 14 December. Both need retrieving in stage 2 to explain the December case peak.

headline: Coronavirus updates to pause from the start of Term 2
detail: In line with the Working Smarter initiative and feedback about email volume, with The Week@UCL continuing and coronavirus emails restarting only as needed.
quote: we are planning to pause these coronavirus emails from the start of next term. You will still receive The Week@UCL every Thursday, and we will restart these coronavirus emails as and when we need to share important information.
notes: The pause did not hold. Issue 129 followed on 5 January 2021, three weeks later, after the third national lockdown was announced. The intention to stop is itself evidence of how UCL read the situation in mid-December.

headline: Phased return of students planned for Term 2 on government guidance
detail: Departments prioritised practical, laboratory and studio subjects and early assessments, with students free to study remotely or on campus.
quote: Departments are writing to students today (Monday 14 December) with information about arrangements for the start of Term Two, in response to recent Government guidance about the phased return of students to universities across the country.
notes: Overtaken within three weeks by the third national lockdown. The plan for a phased return in January never happened as described.

headline: Student study spaces in former offices running at over 80% capacity
detail: Bidborough House, Torrington Place and 1 St Martin's Le Grand given over to study space and the national testing programme.
quote: These study spaces are currently operating at above 80% capacity, and the asymptomatic testing site is playing an important role in supporting our students to travel to and from London more safely.
notes: Evidence that on-campus presence in December 2020 was substantial and concentrated in study space rather than teaching, which is context for the December case figures.

headline: UCL responds to the third national lockdown: work from home if you can
detail: Campus stayed open for estates, libraries, cleaning, catering and security staff, and for researchers needing specialist facilities. Clinically extremely vulnerable staff told not to attend.
quote: If you can work from home during this period, you must do so . However, campus will remain open and some colleagues will be required to work onsite, for example, staff in our estates and libraries teams, and with our cleaning, catering and security partners.
notes: A one-day lag on the announcement of 4 January 2021. This is the policy under which UCL's on-campus student cases fell to their lowest point of the whole series in January 2021, which is the blog post's central claim.

headline: University staff classed as critical workers for school places
detail: Because universities were being asked to stay open and keep delivering learning, even remotely.
quote: Under the latest Government guidance, University staff are considered critical workers and are therefore eligible to send their children to school as usual. This is because we are being asked to keep universities open, and to continue to deliver learning (even if remotely).
notes: Qualified on 1 February: UCL clarified that critical worker status was mainly for school eligibility and did not itself justify travel.

headline: Twice-weekly asymptomatic testing extended to staff working on campus
detail: At Bidborough House, free and voluntary, using lateral flow tests.
quote: UCL and contracted staff who are working on campus and who do not have COVID-19 symptoms are encouraged to get tested twice a week at UCL’s testing centre in Bidborough House.
notes: Five weeks after staff were told not to book asymptomatic tests. Encouraged on 5 January, expected by 18 January. A change in testing intensity that will show in the staff case counts independently of any change in infection.

headline: 2 metre distancing mandated as the default in all settings
detail: Removing the flexibility previously allowed for critical laboratory work, which now needed Head of Department approval and a fresh risk assessment.
quote: In light of the recent increase in coronavirus cases and the tightening of Government restrictions, UCL is now mandating 2-metre social distancing as our default position in all settings, having provided some flexibility for critical lab-based activity if accompanied by a risk assessment.
notes: UCL tightening beyond its own July position, which had already been stricter than the national one metre plus.

headline: UCL legally required to report case figures to Camden Council and the OfS
detail: Alongside responding to cases, informing the testing programme and identifying outbreaks.
quote: report coronavirus case figures to Camden Council and the Office for Students, which we are legally required to do;
notes: The most important provenance fact about the dataset after the case definition itself. The numbers were not a voluntary publication: UCL had a statutory reporting duty to Camden and the OfS, and the public page sat on top of that obligation. The legal basis is a stage 2 retrieval target.

headline: Government redefines a contact as 15 minutes cumulative within two metres
detail: Counting a single period or time accumulated over one day.
quote: Under the new guidance, this now includes anyone who has been within two metres of someone for more than 15 minutes, whether in a single period or cumulatively over the course of one day.
notes: The 15-minute threshold in the national contact definition. The on-campus marker in UCL's published data uses a similar 15-minute rule for presence, which is a different thing measured with a similar rule; do not conflate them.

headline: All UK travel corridors removed and travel restricted to legally permitted reasons
detail: With faculty approval, a risk assessment, TravelCert registration, a negative test up to three days before departure and self-isolation on return.
quote: Staff and students should not travel unless it is for a legally permitted reason . Please note that from today the Government has announced there are no longer any travel corridors .
notes: The tightest travel position of the whole record, and the reversal of the partial reopening of 15 July 2020.

headline: All teaching to remain online for the rest of Term 2
detail: Except a small number of exempt courses, with a no-detriment package being developed for assessment.
quote: In response to the latest guidance from the UK Government , we are now planning for all teaching and other face-to-face activities to remain online for the remainder of Term Two, except for a small number of exempt courses.
notes: The decision that keeps the on-campus student line flat through the Alpha wave. Explicitly a response to national guidance rather than to UCL's own case counts.

headline: Free face masks provided for the commute of staff who must attend campus
detail: From 3 February to 8 March, collectable in Bloomsbury or posted to staff at outlying sites.
quote: UCL will be providing free face masks to wear during your commute from Wednesday 3 February until Monday 8 March when we will review the approach in line with Government guidance .
notes: UCL intervening in the journey to work, which is outside its estate and outside its control, because commuting was the concern staff reported most.

headline: No detriment package published for 2020-21 assessment
detail: Developed with Students' Union UCL.
quote: UCL has today published details of its COVID-19 mitigation measures to support our students through their assessment in 2020-21. We have worked with Students’ Union UCL to develop a ‘no detriment’ package to make sure our students are not disadvantaged by the pandemic.
notes: The second year's version of the principle first adopted on 7 April 2020.

headline: Confirmatory PCR no longer required after a positive lateral flow test
detail: Isolation to begin from the day of the positive lateral flow result.
quote: In line with new Government guidance, anyone who has a positive LFT result no longer needs to take a confirmatory Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test afterwards.
notes: A change in what counts as a confirmed case, and therefore a change in the meaning of the published series partway through it. Lateral flow positives now enter the count without PCR confirmation.

headline: Government roadmap allows practical teaching to resume from 8 March
detail: A four-step roadmap announced on 22 February, with higher education guidance limited at first to practical and practice-based courses needing specialist facilities.
quote: Universities can resume in-person teaching for students on practical or practice-based courses and who require specialist equipment and facilities from 8 March.
notes: Filed on 22 February, the date of the announcement; UCL reported it on 23 February, a one-day lag. The 8 March date is the first loosening for universities since the January lockdown, and it is narrow.

headline: Practical and practice-based teaching resumes on campus
detail: Eligible students contacted directly through their programmes.
quote: As part of the Government’s four-step roadmap to ease lockdown restrictions, from 8 March 2021 UCL can resume in-person teaching for students on practical or practice-based courses and who require specialist equipment.
notes: Filed on 8 March, the effective date; announced 2 March. The blog post notes the shaded campus-closed period running to 17 May 2021, so this partial return sits inside it and should be shown as such rather than as a reopening.

headline: One year of remote working measured in platform use
quote: in the last year, UCL has had 530 Zoom sessions, nearly 40,000 Lecturecast recordings, more than 1.5 million meetings on MS Teams, and over 16 million daily logins on Moodle during term-time
notes: The Zoom figure of 530 is almost certainly wrong by orders of magnitude: issue 119 alone recorded over 2,800 Zoom sessions in a single day in October 2020. Quoted as printed and flagged; do not repeat the 530 figure as a fact.

headline: UCL publishes its own roadmap tracking the government's four steps
detail: More campus spaces from 12 April including fitness, study space and outdoor dining, with a hoped-for full return no earlier than 21 June.
quote: We are now creating our own version of the roadmap for the university, underpinned by our people-first approach and commitment to maintaining our symptom-free testing service and the Connect to Protect reporting tool.
notes: UCL committing to keep its own testing and reporting running through the reopening, which is why the case series continues past the point where campus restrictions ease.

headline: Future of Work survey opened on what should return to campus
detail: A seven-question survey open until 18 April 2021 on what worked remotely and what belongs on site.
quote: What you tell us now will help us decide what areas we should invest in for our future, what changes we should make to how we work and how we can optimise our workspaces to deliver UCL’s ambitions for years to come.
notes: The first question in the record about what should be permanent rather than what should be endured.
